convoluted

/KON-vuh-loo-tid/ - the stress falls on KON · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Convoluted means intricate and complicated.

Explaining the league's convoluted playoff format took the commissioner eleven slides and a decision tree.

Example

The estate's convoluted will sent the lawyers in circles: the house passed to a trust, the trust answered to a foundation, and the foundation's only trustee was the tenant of the house.

Convoluted is more pointed than 'complicated' — from Latin volvere, 'to roll,' it describes something so coiled in on itself that following one thread drags you through every twist of the rest.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

tangled: Tangled is the everyday word for things twisted together into knots — headphone cords, schedules, testimony. Convoluted is the sharper, more formal criticism: it says something was made with too many turns, so that following one thread drags you through every twist of the rest.

circuitous: Circuitous describes a single path that wanders instead of going straight — the long way around, in a drive or an explanation. Convoluted is knottier: nothing about it runs in one line; its parts twist back through one another until the thread is hard to hold.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

streamlined: trimmed until nothing slows it down

simple: having few parts and no twists at all

Where it sits · how tangled and hard to follow — involved → convoluted → labyrinthine

involved vs. convoluted: An involved procedure has many steps but stops short of convoluted — the steps still run in one followable line.

labyrinthine vs. convoluted: Labyrinthine goes further than convoluted: not just twisted but a full maze, built as if to lose you.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — volut-

Root — volut-: rolled (Latin volvere)

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: made to be

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + volut- (rolled) + -ed = rolled up together. Picture a garden hose coiled a dozen times over itself — a convoluted argument loops the very same way.

Use the root in a new word: revolve

Use the root in a new word: revolve: The gallery's newest sculpture revolves, though few visitors stay long enough to notice.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, usually critical

Convoluted criticizes structure: plots, procedures, and explanations with too many turns. Its unit-mate abstruse excuses the material (it runs deep); convoluted blames the maker — this could have been straight, and isn't.
